Every stated count is finite/exhaustive; no finite test is used in place of the infinite theorem. The nonstandard criterion is fully reduced to the cited Theorem 6 and its hypotheses.

originality.rationale: The claim of novelty is the explicitly evaluated simultaneous classification of all 256 binary nearest-neighbor two-channel linear cellular automata and its 56 onsite-basis orbit strata. Searches of the actual parameter class, aliases, exact counts and ranked published research records found no matching evaluated joint census. The general algorithms do not themselves give the exact evaluated population/orbit distributions, which require the finite coefficient incidence and group-action calculation. Historical priority remains provisional, particularly because one earlier matrix-valued paper was only available in abstract.

value.rationale: The 256 ordered rules B+zC are the entire minimal two-component binary span-one linear family, a natural first nonscalar field-based cellular-automaton testbed. The first joint empirical-theorem baseline gives exact strong-transitivity prevalence by temporal entropy and distinguishes 56 onsite-linear equivalence classes, rather than arbitrary slices or textbook yes/no checks. It provides a reproducible reference classification for small algebraic cellular-automaton dynamics; no extension to arbitrary four-symbol automata or all topological conjugacies is claimed.
